⚠️ THE FIRST CHOICE HAD A MISSPELLED ACTIVE AND WAS NOT PUBLISHED. Malcolm originally named candidate _1. Read at native pixels, its jar reads '2% GHD-CU'. The ingredient is GHK-Cu. This is the FOURTH spelling seen on this one ingredient across this project — GHK-CU, GHD-CU, GHB-CU, and now GHD-CU again — which is why every label goes through a native-pixel read rather than a contact-sheet glance.

REPAIRING IT WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED ON A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PREFERENCE. There is precedent: commit 2d48de6 repaired GHB-CU to GHK-CU on the brightening-glow day cream rather than swapping the frame, because GHB is a controlled substance and Malcolm asked for a fix. That repair worked at a 46px cap height with a 7px stroke. HERE the glyph is SEVEN PIXELS TALL in a 1254px frame — at that scale there is no bowl-versus-arms to reconstruct, and any 'K' drawn would be three pixels of invention presented as a correction. So the precedent does not transfer, and the honest move was to surface it and let Malcolm pick a clean sibling.

All six slot-27 candidates were read: _1 is GHD-CU; _2 and _3 are GHK-CU; _4, _5 and _6 are GHK-CU. Malcolm chose #6.

#6'S LABEL WAS THEN READ AT NATIVE PIXELS IN FULL, ALL SIX ELEMENTS CORRECT: the dots-and-dashes helix mark, 'Skingenetix', 'COPPER PEPTIDE', 'ADVANCED DAY REPAIR', 'PREMIUM FORMULA', and '☀ DAY CREAM | 2% GHK-CU | 50ML'. The 2% agrees with the actual catalogue — every copper peptide product on the store states 2%.

THE BLUE CREAM IS CORRECT, NOT A FAULT. GHK-Cu is a copper complex and is genuinely blue; clinical blue is also the scene colour the brand assigns to copper peptide. A white cream here would have been the error.

NOTE ON PRODUCT CHOICE: this is the Copper Peptide day cream appearing in a Glutathione brightening routine. That is consistent with the catalogue — the store's only day gel-cream IS the Copper Peptide (GHK-Cu) Day Gel-Cream — but the jar's artwork says 'ADVANCED DAY REPAIR' where the step is titled 'Day Gel-Cream'.
